newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude closes strong, pre API's.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude closes strong, pre API's.

text.p: August Brent crude on the IPE closed almost one third of a dollar firmer in a technically strong market boosted by market expectations of bullish American Petroleum Institute (API) figures, good fund buying and strong fundamentals, brokers said.

August Brent ended up 31 cents at $18.82 a barrel having followed NYMEX crude and products for most of the afternoon. NYMEX WTI August crude broke through the 40 day moving average on the back of expectations that tonight's figures from the API would show a decline in U.S. crude and gasoline stocks for the week ended June 27.

U.S. crude stocks were expected down one to three million barrels and gasoline stocks off 500,000 to one million barrels. Although distillates were expected to build by one to three million barrels, prompt NYMEX heating oil had gained almost a full cent by the close.
"It makes you feel there are whispers out there on the heating oil. Maybe we are in for a surprise with the API's," one broker said.
IPE July gas oil closed earlier up $2.50 at the days high of $167.75 a tonne in good volume trade.

News implying that Iraqi crude could hit the markets in early August did little to dent the upward move. On Tuesday U.N. humanitarian aid officials said negotiations to finalize an aid distribution plan necessary for resuming Iraqi "oil-for-food" oil sales are running smoothly and should be finalised by week's end.
"They should be done by the end of the week, and be able to send (the aid plan) to New York for the Secretary-General to approve, presumably next week," said an official.
Renewed oil sales were expected to start around two weeks after the distribution plan approval, in late July or early August, the official added.

Physical Brent crude also gained ground on Tuesday as refiners increased their bids for the limited amount of crude available for July. The paper Brent July/August spread reflected the prompt physical tightness, opening on Monday at -11 cents and trading at a staggering +10 cents on Tuesday afternoon.
